evals.prompt: We run a marketplace. Add seller payouts: when an order completes, the seller is owed the order amount minus our 8 percent commission, and we pay sellers weekly in one batch.
evals.expected_output: Payouts modeled as balanced ledger entries (seller payable, commission revenue, cash), balances derived from entries, an idempotent weekly batch, and a trial-balance test.
expectations: Models the completed order as balanced entries: seller payable, commission revenue and the cash or receivable side
Derives the seller balance from entries rather than storing a mutable balance column
Makes the weekly payout batch idempotent by a batch or payout reference
Writes a test that the trial balance is zero after a sequence of orders and payouts

evals.prompt: Loyalty points are redeemable for money in our app. Add expiry: points older than 12 months expire at the end of each month. Start from src/points.py.
evals.expected_output: Treats points as a ledger of earn, redeem and expire entries per lot (first in, first out), with the balance derived and the expiry auditable, and tests around a month end.
expectations: Replaces the mutable points column with append-only entries (earn, redeem, expire)
Expires per earning lot, oldest first, so the expired amount is traceable to the earn it came from
Derives the balance from entries and reconciles any cached value
Tests an expiry at a month end and that redeeming cannot go below zero
